messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] dns_resolver_error_rate high in eu-west-1 · 12% errors over 5m · candidates: Cloudflare resolver pool. Paging oncall.

alex: paging @maria (oncall) — noticing customer 5xx reports too. any initial telemetry? :eyes:

maria (oncall): on it. hitting the cluster now. quick summary: lots of SERVFAIL and some NXDOMAIN from cf-resolvers-eu. Dig shows inconsistent answers across resolvers.

samir: I can repro:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 +short example.service.redwood.net
93.184.216.34
$ dig @eu-resolver.cloudflare.net +short example.service.redwood.net
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @eu-resolver.cloudflare.net example.service.redwood.net +short
; no answer
```

maria (oncall): exactly. Route53 authoritative is healthy from our side (queried directly). Looks like an upstream resolver issue (Cloudflare) + we are seeing a thundering herd of probes amplifying failure surface.

jin: Are customers hitting Cloudflare resolvers specifically? Could be regional peering flap causing retries -> increased qps -> resolver overload.

lisa: CS reports spike in support tickets for API timeouts from EU customers. Some report intermittent DNS failures. Ticket sample: "requests failing intermittently, 502s, then fine after ~20s"

maria (oncall): initial impact: degraded DNS resolution in eu-west-1 -> higher request latency and some failures for any service using public DNS (model endpoints, assets). Broad but not total outage.

alex: mitigation options? We can temporarily prefer Route53 egress for eu-west-1 (bypass Cloudflare), or add aggressive client-side retry/backoff. Which is faster?

samir: fastest is to update GeoDNS weights to steer traffic away from problematic resolver paths for the affected region. Also bump probe TTLs and enable route53-only fallback in our resolver policy.

maria (oncall): I can flip a policy: change geo-dns routing for eu to prefer Route53 authoritative answers (weight -> route53 pool) and reduce health check sensitivity so we don't oscillate. Doing it now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: update geo-dns routing policy id=gw-eu-21 -> new weights to prefer route53 (change set in progress)

maria (oncall): changed. Confirming propagation:
```
$ dig @eu-resolver.cloudflare.net example.service.redwood.net +short
93.184.216.34
$ dig @eu-route53-resolver.example +short example.service.redwood.net
93.184.216.34
```

jin: also pushed a resolver policy to our edge nodes to prefer direct Route53 queries (skip Cloudflare resolver list) for eu-west-1. That reduces dependency on the flaky pool.

lisa: CS: Noticing fewer new tickets after 60s. Customers reporting quicker recovery. :thumbsup:

alex: good. can we quantify traffic shifted and error reduction?

maria (oncall): metrics: dns_error_rate eu-west-1 dropped from 12% -> 1.8% in ~90s. Upstream Cloudflare latency still noisy but traffic routed around it.

samir: set a temporary TTL on critical records to 30s to make rollbacks quicker if needed.

maria (oncall): done. Added status page note: "Partial DNS resolution issues affecting EU customers; mitigation in progress (steering traffic to alternate authoritative path)." cs-ops, please coordinate comms.

cs-ops: copying the note to customers with highest error rates now. Also prepped a templated explanation for SSO and webhooks that rely on DNS.

alex: any downstream risk from steering to Route53-only? e.g., capacity, cache stampede?

samir: Route53 has capacity headroom. Biggest risk: propagation lag for clients with long TTLs — some clients will still hit CF resolvers and see failures until TTL expires. That's why we set low TTL and recommend client retries.

maria (oncall): continuing to monitor. I also opened a ticket with Cloudflare support (case #CF-83421) and included resolver logs/packet captures.

deploy-bot: Rollout finished: geo-dns weights updated, edge resolver policy applied, ttl override set to 30s.

jin: we should schedule a follow-up: examine whether our resolver-backoff was too aggressive (caused herd) and add jitter. Also add passive detection to auto-failover earlier.

lisa: creating a post-incident doc in #postmortems with timeline + external comms. I'll cc product and security for any customer data concerns.

maria (oncall): final check: dns_error_rate eu-west-1 stable at ~0.9% for last 5m. No new P1 tickets. I'll hand off to samir for next shift monitoring and close the page if stable for 30m.

samir: on shift, will watch. thanks.

alex: great job team — short retrospective actions: 1) add jitter to resolver retries, 2) automated geo-dns failover policy, 3) run Chaos test on resolver pools.

incident-bot: Incident resolved? set status -> mitigation applied; monitoring phase started.

maria (oncall): handing off. closing thread once 30m stable. :white_check_mark:
